channel.title: Climate.gov Beyond the Data Blog Posts
channel.description: Climate.gov's Beyond the Data blog posts

item.title: 2024: An active year of U.S. billion-dollar weather and climate disasters
item.description: With Hurricane Helene at the top of the list, there were 27 disasters in the United States in 2024 that individually cost $1 billion or more. It was the second-highest number since the NOAA record…
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Smith

item.title: 2023: A historic year of U.S. billion-dollar weather and climate disasters
item.description: With 28 events, 2023 easily surpassed 2020 as the year with the most billion-dollar disasters in the U.S. The preliminary price tag is at least $92.9 billion.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Smith

item.title: 2022 U.S. billion-dollar weather and climate disasters in historical context
item.description: The country experienced 18 separate billion-dollar weather and climate disasters, tying for third place for the most disasters in a calendar year.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Smith

item.title: Can we expect Atlantic hurricanes to change over the coming century due to global warming?
item.description: Most models project that further warming will decrease the total number of Atlantic hurricanes, but increase the number of very strong storms.
item.dc:creator: Chris Landsea, Tom Knutson

item.title: Can we detect a change in Atlantic hurricanes today due to human-caused climate change?
item.description: Two NOAA hurricane experts explain why it’s still so hard to say whether global warming to date has affected the number or intensity of Atlantic hurricanes.
item.dc:creator: Chris Landsea, Tom Knutson

item.title: 2021 U.S. billion-dollar weather and climate disasters in historical context
item.description: Second-highest in number and third-highest in costs, 2021 was another extreme year for weather and climate disasters in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Smith

item.title: 2020 U.S. billion-dollar weather and climate disasters in historical context
item.description: 2020 smashed the previous record for billion-dollar weather and climate disasters. NCEI's Adam Smith gives us a full accounting of the year's events.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Smith

item.title: 2010-2019: A landmark decade of U.S. billion-dollar weather and climate disasters
item.description: In 2019, the U.S. experienced 14 separate disasters costing at least a billion dollars each. Since 1980, 258 billion-dollar disasters have brought damages in excess of $1.75 trillion.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Smith

item.title: Duct tape and seesaws: Climate trends 101
item.description: With the annual updating of NCEI’s climate trends maps, let’s go Beyond the Data to a land of seesaws and duct tape.
item.dc:creator: Deke Arndt

item.title: Something about lions, lambs, flowers and showers
item.description: First massive flooding and then a blizzard, the Plains and Upper Midwest experienced huge weather events in March and April 2019. In this installment of the Beyond the Data blog, NCEI's Deke Arndt…
item.dc:creator: Deke Arndt
